gap: BHD PASSES the mandatory gate. Same-session, same-data, data-product=bhd-erp, wave sheet deleted (302 rules) vs enabled: /customer 0 of 5,184,000 differing px, /invoice 0 of 5,184,000, mobile dashboard 0 of 1,316,640. Desktop dashboard shows 6,380 of 5,184,000 (0.12%) but every one of them lies in a single band, x 754-906 / y 814-900 css, and cropping both captures shows the SAME donut, SAME red/green/orange, caught at a different animation phase. A control run, two BHD captures under identical conditions with nothing toggled, differs by 5,362 px in that same region, so the A/B sits inside the page's own noise floor. Chart nondeterminism, exempt. Against the stored baseline-*.png the numbers are large (2,437,980 / 307,861 / 953,283 / 597,004) but the customer and invoice figures reproduce r6's to the pixel across two independent rounds, which is stale-baseline data drift, not a leak. So the verdict is design, and it is the SHELL, not the frame. Three measured failures. (1) The topbar: 1364px wide, first painted element at x=922, so 846px, 62.0%, is empty void with hasWordmarkOrTitle=false. r2 measured 760px / 56% four rounds ago; it has got WORSE. Into the remaining 38% go eight controls in four idioms: a search field with a Cmd-K chip, a palette button, a gift button, a button whose own aria-label is 'Interface sound off' rendered as a speaker-with-x (the universal muted/error glyph, sitting permanently in the chrome of a financial app), the word 'English' as text among icons, a globe, a bell with a red '15', and a filled avatar. Wave's header carries its wordmark and one gift icon, and hands the page a large confident 'Transactions'. (2) The rail's active state on the FRONT DOOR. On /customer it is now exactly right, one item tinted, rgba(43,87,216,0.08), blue icon in a pale-blue rounded square, on the page you are on; r6's saturated-blue-on-the-wrong-item is genuinely fixed there. But on / the rail paints TWO, and the stronger one, rgba(43,87,216,0.11), is on 'Favorites', a submenu CONTAINER, not a page, at y=74 h=42, while the current page 'Dashboard' gets the weaker 0.08 on a box measuring 0x0 at y=0. So on the first screen anyone sees, the only visible 'you are here' pill points at a folder and the actual page's marker has no rendered area at all. r2 named the Favorites confusion; five rounds later the front door still has it. (3) The dashboard's number ink: eight figures in four colours, rgb(43,87,216) blue, rgb(21,128,61) green, rgb(180,35,24) red, rgb(16,24,40) near-black, and '0.000' renders GREEN in one tile and RED in another. A zero is neither good news nor bad news. The bar's whole table runs on two ink weights, bold near-black primary and muted grey secondary. Smaller: Payroll and Banking quick actions carry the identical classical-building glyph, which is also a rail item and the 'Business Health' section marker; and 'Price Calculator Description' is literal placeholder copy shipping on the front door. The list-page table, the #f5f9ff ground, the Plus Jakarta Sans sans-serif headings and the rounded white container ARE bar-grade or better, and on /customer alone ours would win. The frame is finished. The furniture in it, and the front door specifically, is not, so it does not CLEARLY win.
